items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: I didn't play with Ed Carey, they were a little older than I was, you know. I was a little boy, they wouldn't let me in

ctx.x: She loved her. She was a tremendous entertainer. Just a tremendous entertainer. But I had -- I don't know how I could have forgotten Albert Topps because it was a very important time in my life too. Because Albert -- they -- we had another drummer working there with us by the name of Bill Winston who was quite a musician. He played with Scoops' brother's band, Ed Carey. They had a band in Chicago. I didn't play with Ed Carey, they were a little older than I was, you know. I was a little boy, they wouldn't let

me in, you know.

But Scoops wasn't much older than I was, but he got in because it was his brother, you know. But Bill Winston is now living in Hawaii, he's in Honolulu, and he's the president -- he was the president of the union, the musician's union there now. But I don't think he is now, he's still affiliated with the union in some capacity. As a matter of fact I was over there last year with Hubert Laws. We did a couple of concerts at the University of Hawaii and I saw Bill Winston. Now, in the band was with…
